note: The corpus's assertions that are red at HEAD, each owned by an open task. This is a NAMED LIST and deliberately not a ceiling: a ceiling lets one task pay the debt and the next task spend it, which is the reasoning cli/test/assertion-debt.test.mjs was built on. Every entry here is a case the suite reports rather than fails on — so it can live in the gate without crying wolf (docs/agents/cli.md) while still holding the assertion the SH338 order says must land before the fix. The list is checked in BOTH directions: an entry whose assertion has gone green FAILS the run, naming the id to delete. That is what stops the list becoming the place findings go to be forgotten.
tier: SH671 — an entry names the tier that can observe it: `fast` for the offline chain in cli/test/source-corpus.test.mjs, `live` for the socket in cli/conformance/source-corpus.conformance.mjs. Absent means `fast`, which is what every entry written before the field would have been. The scope is not bookkeeping: each tier checks its OWN entries in both directions, and without it the two would report each other's keys as unexercised — a stale-key failure meaning only that the other driver did not run. The live tier had no holding() call at all until SH671, so a socket-only red had nowhere to be declared and sat undeclared in a gate; fixtures/source-sites/open-findings.mjs is the one implementation both tiers read, because a ledger whose two readers can disagree about what held means is the SH245 defect with the stakes of a gate.
rule: SH568 — an entry must name a BEHAVIOUR, never a mechanism. `layout-raw-field-CSS` read 'the generated layout does not emit {{CSS}} with two braces', which pinned one implementation of a fix; the cure landed on the value instead (Handlebars.SafeString), the defect closed, and the both-directions check then held a CORRECT repair as a permanent red. An entry phrased as 'the code does not do X' can only go green the one way its author imagined. Phrase it as what a reader, a page or a gate would observe, and the assertion survives whichever repair lands.
